newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks end higher after hitting new highs.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks end higher after hitting new highs.

text.p: Australian shares swaggered to a higher close on Thursday, defying a wobbly Wall Street and hitting new highs in the afternoon session before easing back.
The All Ordinaries index reached a record high of 2,429.2, surpassing the previous record high of 2,426.5 reached on December 31, 1996.
However, the benchmark failed to break its record close of 2,424.6, adding 8.2 points to 2,423.2 by the end of the day.

"The market generally firmed in every sector except gold which is still struggling," said director of institutions at Ord Minnett, Eric Gale, adding that an upbeat attitude to base metals had helped the market consolidate its late 1996 gains.

"Sentiment has changed for the better for the base metals. We have had a rise in copper stocks but the copper price continued to go up despite that, and we've had a good snapback in nickel and aluminium," Gale said.
"The only laggard is gold at the present time and sentiment for it is appalling at the moment," he added.
Major corporate news of the day was CRA selling its controversial Century zinc project in north Queensland to major zinc producer, Pasminco, for A$345 million (US$269 million).
Pasminco shares closed marginally lower at A$1.92 amid uncertainty over native title issues and possible capital raisings to fund the deal.
"I would say the market regards it as a reasonable deal for both sides," Gale said, noting the importance of Century ore to Pasminco's Budel smelter in the Netherlands.
"If you see Pasminco a little weaker, the market may have already put it in a cum-rights situation but it is only off a little," he said.

Major miner WMC continued its run from Wednesday, its shares closing 12 cents higher at A$8.07 as nickel prices held up. It received a further boost when its 39.25 percent owned Alcoa Australia announced a 15 percent higher net profit of A$395 million for the 1996 calendar year.

The good news from the second tier oil companies continued with shares in Petroleum Securities leaping 40 cents to A$6.65 after it announced a new discovery in its U.S. oil and gas fields in the Gulf of Mexico.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about seven to six, while about 32 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
